findings.problem: fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap() panics on I/O errors (file not found, permission denied, etc.)
findings.failure_mode: untrusted or missing file paths abort the entire program instead of returning a typed I/O error
findings.fix: return Result<Vec<Record>, io::Error> and use ? to propagate, or map_err to a domain error

findings.failure_mode: malformed CSV lines crash the program instead of yielding a typed ParseError per record
findings.fix: return Result<Vec<Record>, ParseError> and use ? on parse, returning per-record errors rather than panicking

findings.problem: as u16 is a lossy cast from u32 to u16; values > 65535 silently truncate
findings.failure_mode: out-of-range values wrap around instead of being rejected as invalid domain data
findings.fix: use u16::try_from(value) and return an error on overflow

findings.problem: split(',').map(...).collect() allocates a Vec of all parts; split_once suffices for two-field records
findings.failure_mode: unnecessary heap allocation per line, and no bounds checking on parts length before indexing
findings.fix: use line.split_once(',') to get (name, rest) directly, then parse rest from the second half

findings.problem: parts[0] unchecked indexing into Vec without verifying len >= 1
findings.failure_mode: empty lines or lines with no comma panic with index-out-of-bounds
findings.fix: use split_once(',') and pattern-match the Option, returning Err for missing fields

findings.problem: parts[1] unchecked indexing into Vec without verifying len >= 2
findings.failure_mode: lines with only one comma-separated field panic with index-out-of-bounds
findings.fix: use the second binding from split_once(',') which is an Option that must be handled

findings.problem: println!() is hidden I/O/side-effect inside a data-loading function that should be pure parsing
findings.failure_mode: side effects are not observable in the type signature, cannot be controlled or tested independently, and pollute the parsing layer with shell concerns
findings.fix: remove println! from the parsing logic; logging belongs in the imperative shell at the call site

findings.problem: load_sessions mixes I/O (fs::read_to_string), parsing, and domain construction in one function
findings.failure_mode: pure parsing cannot be unit-tested in isolation; I/O errors, parse errors, and domain errors are conflated into a Vec with no error distinction
findings.fix: split into (1) pure parse_records(&[str]) -> Result<Vec<Record>, ParseError> and (2) shell function load_sessions(path) -> Result<Vec<Record>, Error> that reads and delegates

findings.problem: Vec<Record> return with no try_reserve and no bounded capacity handling
findings.failure_mode: allocation failure in hot path silently panics via unwrap on collect, or grows unboundedly on malicious input
findings.fix: return Result<Vec<Record>, AllocationError>, use try_reserve with checked_mul for record count budget, and handle allocation failure gracefully

findings.problem: value: u16 is a raw primitive that accepts any u16 value including domain-invalid ranges
findings.failure_mode: no type-level invariant enforces valid value ranges; domain rules are not enforced by the type system
findings.fix: introduce a newtype e.g. pub struct Value(u16) with a fallible constructor that validates the domain range

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists for load_sessions throughput or allocation profile
no profiler data for per-line allocation patterns (split + collect + to_string)
no allocation audit (no try_reserve, no capacity budget on Vec growth)
no second-ring analysis for downstream consumers of Record
no command evidence (cargo test, cargo clippy, cargo bench) was run
residual_risk: This is a static review with no commands executed. The function has 9 independent blocker violations: unhandled I/O errors, unhandled parse errors, lossy cast, unchecked indexing, hidden I/O side-effect, missing type safety for domain values, unbounded allocation, and no functional core/shell split. Every path that processes untrusted input can panic. The crate must be reworked before any delivery gate.
